chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A single dirham of usury is more severe than seventy acts of adultery, all of them with a close relative.

key_terms.بِذَاتِ مَحْرَمٍ: With a close relative (with whom marriage is permanently forbidden)
key_terms.زَنْيَةً: An act of illicit sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: How does the severity of a small amount of usury compare to adultery in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the spiritual gravity of riba by comparing a single dirham of it to seventy acts of zina with a close relative, emphasizing its pervasive corruption of wealth and soul. This comparison underscores the severity of riba not merely as a financial transaction but as a major sin that disrupts social and spiritual equilibrium, a view supported by Shia jurists who often cite this narration to highlight the distinct weight of usury in moral theology. The reference to 'seventy' mirrors other major sins in Islamic tradition, suggesting a cumulative or comprehensive severity that affects both individual piety and communal economic justice.
